title: Giving Feedback by Offering to Help
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This piece describes an indirect feedback technique: instead of naming a performance problem directly, a leader frames the same critique as an offer of assistance. Using the example of a chronically late colleague, it contrasts a blunt statement about punctuality with the softer alternative, "What can I do to help you arrive to our meetings on time?", which conveys the same message with less sting. The author argues this approach works especially well with people who are feedback-sensitive or have heard the same criticism repeatedly without changing. It notes two practical strengths of the technique: virtually any feedback can be reframed this way, and a leader can repeat the same offer of help multiple times without appearing demanding.
points: Reframing feedback as an offer of help reduces defensiveness while still communicating the underlying performance concern clearly.
The technique is particularly effective with people who are highly sensitive to criticism or have repeatedly ignored more direct feedback.
Nearly any piece of feedback can be converted into a help-offering framing, making it a broadly reusable tool.
A leader can repeat the same offer of assistance multiple times without it reading as nagging or demanding.
quotes: Asking others how you might help them can be a highly indirect and effective way of giving feedback.
In this example, the leader might say, “What can I do to help you arrive to our meetings on time? Your performance is suffering, and I would like to help.
By expressing the feedback indirectly by offering assistance, the leader makes the message more about their desire to lend a hand and less about the infraction of lateness.
Giving feedback by offering help can be highly effective, especially for those who are sensitive to feedback or have heard the same criticisms multiple times but simply fail to make changes.
Second, a leader can offer the same help over and over without appearing petulant or demanding, keeping the feedback fresh and present.
